newsitem.title: USA: Man's nose amputated by human bite.
newsitem.headline: Man's nose amputated by human bite.

text.p: A brawl on a holiday cruise ship turned vicious on Monday, leaving one man without a nose and other men held in suspicion of biting it off.
Coast Guard officials said they responded to the emergency shortly after midnight Monday morning after receiving a call from the doctor on the ship, which was sailing off the coast of San Diego.
"He said he had a patient on board whose nose had been amputated by a human bite," Coast Guard spokeswoman Jamie Devitt said.

The patient, 28-year-old Scott Irvine of Long Beach, California, was rushed to a hospital where he underwent surgery to reattach the nose. Hospital officials said it was too early to comment on the success of the operation.
The Coast Guard said details on the events preceding the bite were sketchy, but that others on the ship reported Irvine was involved in an altercation with two other men.
Police met the ship at its berth to investigate and detained potential suspects.
